title: Finite-stage supported generators and their actual derived scalar images
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. On profinite sets with finite jointly surjective covers put
$$C(S)=\{f\in C(S,\Omega):f(S)\subset E\text{ for some finite }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E\subset\Omega\},\quad B(S)=C(S,\Omega),\quad A_E(S)=C(S,E).$$
Use the condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], their coefficient pullbacks $R_T=p_T^*R$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(R_T)$ of internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Constructible always means finite constant local models on a finite constructible locally closed stratification [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and lisse means finite free on a pro-étale cover [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. For a locally closed immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ define $a_!=i_*j_!$ for an open-then-closed factorization $a=i\circ j$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star].

For every coefficient inclusion $R\to R'$ among $A_E\to C$, $C\to B$ and $A_E\to B$, put $T_T^{R,R'}=R'_T\otimes^L_{R_T}-$, computed on K-flat resolutions [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. These functors are exact for the triangulated structures. Their right adjoints are exact termwise restrictions of scalars, with shift-compatible unit represented by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$. They agree with derived extension for section-module sheaves under the canonical equivalence with internal modules. For every such $a$ and every $K\in D(R_S)$ there is a natural $R'_X$-linear isomorphism
$$T_X^{R,R'}(a_!K)\cong a_!T_S^{R,R'}K.$$
For lisse $R_S$-modules $L$, $T_S^{R,R'}L[0]\cong(R'_S\otimes_{R_S}L)[0]$ is lisse in degree zero; these comparisons respect the transitivity $A_E\to C\to B$ of scalar extension and inverse image.

Let $\mathcal G_C$ consist of all
$$G_{a,E,L}=a_!(C_S\otimes^L_{A_{E,S}}L[0]),$$
where $a$ varies over constructible locally closed immersions, $E$ over finite intermediate fields, and $L$ over lisse $A_{E,S}$-modules. Every $G_{a,E,L}$ is bounded constructible, and $D^b_c(X,C)$ is exactly the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory of $D(C_X)$ containing $\mathcal G_C$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Each object is obtainable from zero and finitely many such generators by finitely many integer shifts and distinguished-triangle extensions. For the specified $J_X=T_X^{C,B}$ the generator comparison is
$$J_XG_{a,E,L}\cong a_!(B_S\otimes_{A_{E,S}}L)[0].$$
The scheme $X$ is Noetherian and every locally closed scheme $S\hookrightarrow X$ is again separated of finite type over $k$. Empty schemes, empty supports and rank zero are included. No flatness of a coefficient inclusion is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover of X as in the finite-type definition. Each coordinate algebra is finitely generated over k and hence Noetherian by lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components. Thus X is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. Every closed subscheme of X has affine charts Spec(A/I), finitely generated over k. Every open of such a closed subscheme is quasi-compact, so a finite affine refinement by principal opens has finitely generated coordinate algebras (A/I)[1/f]. Consequently every locally closed S is again finite type and Noetherian. It is separated: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of X over k, since an immersion is a monomorphism. On affine charts the required closed immersions are quotient maps; their base changes are quotient maps and their composites are quotient maps. Thus these assertions hold for arbitrary subscheme structures, including empty S. All complements of the immersions used below are quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; finite-type affine-chart verification; definitions of open and closed immersions

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction to each of the three ring maps on each scheme T. The reconstructed section-ring sheaves have exactly the same scalar units as the internal rings. In those section categories lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings gives the everywhere-defined triangulated scalar functor, computed on K-flat resolutions. The specified derived adjunction and its actual unit are those of lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction. Transport back gives T_T and exact termwise scalar restriction. On a K-flat representative P the unit is P→Res(R'_T⊗P), v↦1⊗v. For P[n] the same formula in degree q is the formula on P^{q+n}; the differential on both sides is multiplied by (-1)^n. K-flat representatives remain K-flat under shifts. Hence this is the shift-compatible unit for the indicated canonical shift structures. This proves the first scalar assertions, including agreement with section-module derived extension, without asserting exactness of ordinary scalar extension.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); internal comparison: sites-modules.tex Tags 03EK and 0GMW

proof.text: For a lisse R_S-module L, pass through the exact section equivalence. Pulling its trivializing pro-etale cover back to an arbitrary site object gives the covering hypothesis of lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars. That lemma makes L[0] K-flat and identifies derived scalar extension with (R'_S⊗L)[0], locally (R'_S)^{r}. The internal comparison of step 2 returns this as an R'_S-linear isomorphism. For any scheme inverse image use lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization; its lambda gives the natural scalar/pullback comparison. In section coordinates it is the balanced pullback map of lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization, which also states its composition and identity compatibilities. This gives inverse-image compatibility on the full unbounded categories, not just on the lisse objects.

Let j:U→T be open. Work in section-module categories using lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport. The functors j_!, j^* are exact and adjoint by lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed, so their termwise derived functors have the localized adjunction of def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction. For K in D(R_U) and N in D(R'_T) the successive specified adjunctions give
Hom(T_T j_! K,N) ≅ Hom(j_!K,Res_T N) ≅ Hom(K,j_R^*Res_T N)
≅ Hom(K,Res_U j_{R'}^*N) ≅ Hom(T_U K,j_{R'}^*N) ≅ Hom(j_!T_U K,N).
The middle comparison is the identity on underlying restricted sheaves and maps, with the same R_U-action because both coefficient maps are pulled back from the point. Both functors are therefore left adjoint to Res_U j_{R'}^*. The unique unit-compatible isomorphism of lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation gives T_T j_!≅j_!T_U. It lies in D(R'_T), so is R'_T-linear, and is natural in K.

Let i:Z→T be closed, with complementary open j. Set H=T_T(i_*K). Scalar/pullback compatibility from step 3 and the mixed vanishing j^*i_*=0 give j^*H=0. The actual closed unit is therefore an isomorphism H→i_*i^*H by lem-sfb-condensed-support-derived-localization for R'. Now i^*H≅T_Z(i^*i_*K)≅T_ZK, by scalar/pullback compatibility and the closed counit for R. Their composite gives the required natural R'_T-linear isomorphism T_T i_*K≅i_*T_ZK. This argument uses the unbounded support statement, not a bounded-below recollement. For a=i∘j in the stated open-then-closed factorization, apply first this closed comparison and then i_* of step 4. The result is T_X a_!K≅a_!T_SK for every K.

For a scalar tower R→R'→R'', restrictions compose by the identity on underlying complexes and actions. Both T^{R',R''}T^{R,R'} and T^{R,R''} are left adjoint to this composite restriction. Choose their unique unit-compatible isomorphism. Its unit is the composite v↦1⊗v↦1⊗(1⊗v); thus on balanced representatives its contraction is c⊗(b⊗v)↦cb⊗v. For a longer tower both contractions preserve this same composite unit, hence are equal by uniqueness. The inverse-image comparisons are mates of the underlying identity restriction squares, by lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization. The open comparison in step 4 is the corresponding conjugate. Mate pasting therefore makes these comparisons compatible with the scalar-tower contractions. For the closed comparison in step 5, its defining composite is the closed unit followed by i_* of lambda and the closed counit. Pasting those naturality squares gives the same composite for either tower path: lambda pastes by mate pasting, and the adjacent unit/counit pair cancels by the adjunction identity. Equivalently, apply the fully faithful closed restriction to these maps between supported objects; both become the same scalar/pullback tower map. This proves the claimed transitivity compatibilities, including for a_!=i_*j_!.

source.place: (3), scalar transitivity and compatibility; canonical comparison normalized by composite adjunction units

proof.text: For each G_{a,E,L}, step 3 for A_E→C identifies its inner derived object with a lisse C_S-module M in degree zero. Thus G≅(a_!M)[0], and lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-lisse-extension-constructible puts G in D^b_c(X,C). Conversely, det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation for the bounded-image condensed coefficient ring C expresses every object of D^b_c(X,C) by finitely many cones and shifts from a_!M with M lisse over C_S. The S of each generator satisfies the standing scheme assumptions by step 1. Clause (1) of sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit applied on S supplies a finite E and lisse A_{E,S}-module L with C_S⊗L≅M. Step 3 identifies this ordinary scalar extension with its derived version, hence this supported generator is isomorphic to G_{a,E,L}. No assertion about finite-field descent over the all-continuous ring B is used.

source.place: Converse, Single sheaves and Complexes; finite-stage replacement uses sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit proof (1)

proof.text: The finite constructions in step 7 belong to any full replete triangulated subcategory containing the specified generators. Conversely D^b_c(X,C) is itself such a subcategory by det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated. These two inclusions prove the asserted smallest-subcategory equality. Cones can be expressed as distinguished-triangle extensions after rotation: for f:A→B, the rotated cone triangle has vertices B, Cone(f), A[1]. Thus the finite cones and shifts in step 7 give precisely finite shifts and triangle extensions from zero and finitely many G's. The zero object is allowed initially; for empty X this supplies the entire zero category, and no positive-rank or nonempty-support hypothesis has entered.

source.place: Converse and final induction; elementary rotation and finite-assembly consequence

proof.text:
Finally, apply step 5 to J_X=T_X^{C,B} and the specified generator. Step 6 contracts the scalar tower and step 3 computes its lisse input:
J_XG_{a,E,L} ≅ a_! T_S^{C,B}T_S^{A_E,C}L[0] ≅ a_!T_S^{A_E,B}L[0] ≅ (a_!(B_S⊗_{A_{E,S}}L))[0].
These are isomorphisms in D(B_X), not merely isomorphisms of individual cohomology sheaves. Their tower and inverse-image compatibilities are exactly those checked in steps 3 and 6. For L=0 every tensor and extension is zero; on an empty support every extension is zero. This also verifies the stated rank-zero and empty-support cases.
